label: GPT-6 Astra
output:
Tolu, me o 😂 I’m literally the person you’re looking for. I wrote JAMB in 2025, scored 251, applied for Medicine and Surgery and got Biology instead. I’m in a federal university here in Lagos, currently Biology 100L. So let me tell you my own experience, but please don’t take my school’s rules as your school’s rules.

First, I understand the crying. The day I saw Biology on my portal, I locked myself inside my cousin’s room in Surulere and cried. I didn’t eat. I had already pictured myself doing Medicine, so seeing Biology felt like everything had scattered. My mum was still telling people in church that I was doing Medicine for like two months 😭 I had to actually beg her to stop. It’s funny small now, but at the time it wasn’t funny at all.

So please don’t let anybody make you feel ungrateful because you’re disappointed. You can know that admission is hard to get and still be pained that you didn’t get what you wanted. Both can be true.

Now, the transfer matter. Kingsley, I understand that nobody you know transferred, but saying transfer is a myth is not correct. It happens. At the same time, favour’s “just read hard” is making it sound simpler than it is.

**What our level adviser told us is that to transfer to MBBS after 100L, you need at least 4.5 CGPA out of 5, AND there must be space.** That “and” is very important. It’s not that once you get 4.5, they must move you. You can meet the academic requirement and still have the space issue to contend with.

According to our adviser, about six people got moved into Medicine from the whole faculty last year. She thinks over 40 people applied. I didn’t personally see the list of applicants, so I’m telling you what she told us, not presenting it like statistics I verified myself. But it should give you an idea of why nobody should promise you a transfer.

She also said you need to meet the Medicine cut-offs in JAMB and post-UTME too. So your 268 on its own doesn’t settle whether you’re eligible. I don’t know your school’s Medicine cut-offs or your post-UTME score. Please check both. Don’t let somebody just look at 268 and tell you, “Ah, you’re fine, enter first.”

And let me not come here and form academic weapon for you: my own CGPA after first semester is **4.31**. Not 4.5. I’m still trying. I want you to know that because it’s easy to tell somebody “just get 4.5” when you’re not the one writing the exams. Wanting Medicine very badly doesn’t automatically make the grades come.

For our 100L courses, we have BIO 101, CHM 101, PHY 101, MTH 101 and GST. So if you’re imagining that Biology means you’ll only be reading about plants and animals, no o. Physics and maths are the ones dealing with people. You still need to take all those courses seriously, especially if you’re chasing a high CGPA.

There are practical expenses too. My lab coat was ₦6,500, dissecting kit was ₦9,000, and practical manual was extra. Those are my own costs, not a price list for your school, but it’s something to keep in mind apart from acceptance fee and school fees.

As for whether Biology is bad, honestly, no. I’m enjoying parts of it much more than I expected, especially genetics and cell biology. At first I was looking at everything through “but this is not Medicine,” so I wasn’t even giving the course a fair chance.

Our first BIO practical, we dissected toads. One guy in my group fainted, and I was fine. That was the day I caught myself actually being interested in what we were doing. Like, wait, I actually like this thing? 😂 It didn’t suddenly erase my Medicine plans, but it made me realise that being disappointed with the admission and disliking the course are not necessarily the same thing.

That’s why I wouldn’t tell you Biology is bad just because it wasn’t your first choice. But I also won’t tell you that because I’m beginning to enjoy it, you must enjoy it too. Biology is its own course. You need to consider it as something you might actually finish, not just somewhere to sit for one year before MBBS.

Ask yourself this one honestly: **if the transfer doesn’t happen, would I be willing to continue Biology?** You don’t have to be excited about that possibility immediately, but you shouldn’t pretend it doesn’t exist. If the only reason you’re accepting is that your dad believes transfer is guaranteed, please confirm the rules together before making that decision.

On rewriting, I don’t think it’s wrong either. If Medicine is genuinely what you want and you’re ready to prepare again, that is a valid choice. But “one year is nothing” is easier to say from outside.

My secondary school classmate Ifeoma rejected Pharmacy to rewrite for Medicine. She has written JAMB two more times and is still at home. I’m not telling you that to scare you or say your own will go like hers. It’s just why I can’t casually tell somebody, “Reject it, you’ll get Medicine next year.” Nobody knows that. Staying home and facing another admission cycle is not always easy, and rewriting isn’t a guarantee any more than transfer is.

Since your acceptance fee deadline is coming up, my strongest advice is to go to your own faculty/department now and ask for the exact transfer rules. Ask whether Biology students can apply for MBBS transfer, the required CGPA, the JAMB and post-UTME requirements, how spaces are decided and what happens if you qualify but aren’t selected. If there are written guidelines, ask to see them. Don’t base this decision on forum people, including me. I can tell you my experience, but I can’t confirm your school’s policy.

Also, when you’ve calmed down small, ask yourself whether you really want to study and practise Medicine, or whether part of what is hurting is losing the “doctor” title you and your parents had already imagined. I’m not saying your dream isn’t yours. I had to think about that too, especially with my mum still announcing Medicine in church. Try to separate what you want from what everybody is expecting of you.

I won’t choose for you. Accepting Biology isn’t automatically giving up, and rewriting isn’t automatically wasting time. Just make either decision with the real possibilities in front of you, not somebody’s promise.

Sorry, this is long, but I wish somebody had explained it properly to me too. Cry if you need to, then get the information before the deadline. Whatever you choose, this admission outcome is not the end of your world, Tolu. ❤️
